output.summary: A herbaceous elder native to southern and central Europe and southwest Asia, dwarf elder forms large groups of upright stems from an extensive underground stem. It bears flat-topped clusters of white, occasionally pink, flowers and glossy black berries. All parts are toxic, especially the seeds, though cooking can neutralize the toxicity.
output.edibilityNote: All parts are toxic, especially the seeds, but cooking can neutralize the toxicity; explicit human food use is not described.
